notes: §1985:XIV.3.6.4 GR6: format 1 releases one portion, format 2 never more than one message or segment, and "the MCS will not transmit any portion of a message to a communication device until the entire message has been released to the MCS". Dialogue.Release appends a portion, closes a segment on ESI and returns a StoredMessage only on EMI/EGI, which SendToDestinations enqueues and SendToTerminal transmits, so nothing reaches a device or queue before the message ends. Witness: portion/ESI/EMI counts 0,0,1 and a device file written only after EMI. Probes at --std 85: (e) device destination: three portions (format 1 twice, identifier-2=1) leave DEV.out absent; portions+ESI+EMI+EGI write HEHEHEL then H; a run ending with an ESI-only message writes nothing; I-O CD terminal written once (HEHEHE) after EMI; LOOP+DEV destinations: SEG count 0, EMI count 1, DEV gets HEHE then HE; (b) disabled destination 10/key 2, unknown 20/key 1, DESTINATION COUNT 0 status 30, nothing released.

next.reason: 1985: "A single execution of a SEND statement represented by format 2 never releases to the MCS more than a single message or a single message segment"; 2023: "SEND only sends a message to a message server run unit: "A message is sent to the run unit identified by the content of literal-1 or message-server-name-1"". 2023 drops the 1985 communication SEND with segments, ESI/EMI/EGI and MCS release. Its SEND is a message-server SEND between run units, and no candidate keeps the release rule.
